aomNorseRumor0.text: Tundra Titans, Ymir Frost Giants and Ginnungagap Titans are the mightiest Norse creatures.

aomNorseRumor1.text: I hear the Norse plant Yggdrasil at the heart of their town to honor the hero who brought them the Grail.

aomNorseRumor2.text: The Norse fight by position: Berserkers and Throwing Axemen stand shoulder to shoulder in a shield wall, and arrows hurt far less.

aomNorseRumor3.text: When a Norse stack has allies on both rear diagonals, it hacks extra hard that round; veterans call it the Svinfylking.

aomNorseRumor4.text: Norse heroes remember those who fall in battle; once enough are stored, Valhalla sends a band of Einherjar back to help.

aomNorseRumor5.text: How many stars light up at the start of battle depends on the levels of the Norse troops in the army; when all seven are lit, Ragnarok comes from round 7.

aomNorseRumor6.text: Bearskin Berserkers grow wilder the more they are hurt: once a stack drops below half its health, they hit half again as hard.

aomNorseRumor7.text: The Ymir Frost Giant strikes with its freezing blow only once per battle; whoever it hits cannot move for the rest of that round and the whole next one.

aomNorseRumor8.text: The Fenris Pack never hunts alone: for every other kind of allied wolf beside it, it bites harder.

aomNorseRumor9.text: Storm Krakens love capsizing big targets: against two-hex enemies they deal a quarter more damage.

aomNorseRumor10.text: Valkyrie Choosers not only heal those around them, but sometimes raise those who have just fallen.

aomNorseRumor11.text: Once the Mead Hall opens in a Norse town, six more Berserkers come each week.

aomNorseRumor12.text: They say the Dwarven Armory in Norse towns builds Battering Rams every week, for gold only.

aomNorseRumor13.text: Four kinds of giants live in the snowy mountains: Mountain, Rock, Frost and Fire. Whoever brings their hearts back to the Jotun Altar benefits the whole kingdom.
